verses.zh: 有话说：人若休妻，妻离他而去，作了别人的妻，前夫岂能再收回她来？若收回她来，那地岂不是大大玷污了吗？但你和许多亲爱的行邪淫，还可以归向我。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: “If a man divorces his wifeand she leaves him and becomes another man’s wife,he may not take her back again.[NOTE:1] Doing that would utterly defile the land.[NOTE:2] But you, Israel, have given yourself as a prostitute to many gods.[NOTE:3] So what makes you think you can return to me?”[NOTE:4] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “May he go back to her again?” The question is rhetorical and expects a negative answer.sn For the legal background for the illustration that is used here, see Deut 24:1-4.
Heb “Would the land not be utterly defiled?” The stative is here rendered actively to connect better with the preceding. The question is rhetorical and expects a positive answer.
Heb “But you have played the prostitute with many lovers.”

Heb “Returning to me.” The form is the bare infinitive, which the KJV and ASV have interpreted as an imperative: “Yet, return to me!” However, it is more likely that a question is intended, expressing surprise in the light of the law alluded to and the facts cited. For the use of the infinitive absolute in the place of a finite verb, cf. GKC 346 §113.ee. For the introduction of a question without a question marker, cf. GKC 473 §150.a.

verses.zh: 你向净光的高处举目观看，你在何处没有淫行呢？你坐在道旁等候，好像阿拉伯人在旷野埋伏一样，并且你的淫行邪恶玷污了全地。
verses.en: “Look up at the hilltops and consider this.[NOTE:1] Where have you not been ravished?[NOTE:2] You waited for those gods like a thief lying in wait in the wilderness.[NOTE:3] You defiled the land by your wicked prostitution to other gods.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “and see.”

The rhetorical question expects the answer “nowhere,” which asserts the widespread nature of the nation’s idolatry. The prophets often compare Judah’s religious infidelity, idolatry, to adultery or prostitution. Jeremiah goes a step further in exposing their folly by portraying their willing acts of idolatry as being sexually violated.
Heb “You sat for them [the lovers, i.e., the foreign gods] beside the road like an Arab in the desert.”
Heb “by your prostitution and your wickedness.” This is probably an example of hendiadys where, when two nouns are joined by “and,” one expresses the main idea and the other qualifies it.

verses.zh: 因此甘霖停止，春（原文是晚）雨不降。你还是有娼妓之脸，不顾羞耻。
verses.en: That is why the rains have been withheldand the spring rains have not come.Yet in spite of this you are obstinate as a prostitute.[NOTE:1] You refuse to be ashamed of what you have done.
notes: Heb “you have the forehead of a prostitute.”

verses.zh: 从今以后，你岂不向我呼叫说：我父啊，你是我幼年的恩主。
verses.en: Even now you say to me, ‘You are my father![NOTE:1] You have been my faithful companion ever since I was young.
notes: Heb “Have you not just now called out to me, ‘[You are] My father!’?” The rhetorical question expects a positive answer.

verses.zh: 耶和华岂永远怀怒，存留到底吗？看哪，你又发恶言又行坏事，随自己的私意而行（或译：你虽这样说，还是行恶放纵欲心）。
verses.en: You will not always be angry with me, will you?You will not be mad at me forever, will you?’[NOTE:1] That is what you say,but you continually do all the evil that you can.”[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Will he keep angry forever? Will he maintain [it] to the end?” The questions are rhetorical and expect a negative answer. The change to direct address in the English translation is intended to ease the problem of the rapid transition, common in Hebrew style (but not in English), from second person direct address in the preceding lines to third person indirect address in these two lines. See GKC 462 §144.p.
Heb “You do the evil and you are able.” This is an example of hendiadys, meaning, “You do all the evil that you are able to do.”

verses.zh: 约西亚王在位的时候，耶和华又对我说：「背道的以色列所行的，你看见没有？她上各高山，在各青翠树下行淫。
verses.en: When Josiah was king of Judah, the Lord said to me, “Jeremiah, you have no doubt seen what wayward Israel has done.[NOTE:1] You have seen how she went up to every high hill and under every green tree to give herself like a prostitute to other gods.[NOTE:2]
notes: “Have you seen…” The question is rhetorical and expects a positive answer.

Heb “she played the prostitute there.” This is a metaphor for Israel’s worship; she gave herself to the worship of other gods like a prostitute gives herself to her lovers. There seems no clear way to completely spell out the metaphor in the translation.

verses.zh: 她行这些事以后，我说她必归向我，她却不归向我。她奸诈的妹妹犹大也看见了。
verses.en: Yet even after she had done all that, I thought that she might come back to me.[NOTE:1] But she did not. Her sister, unfaithful Judah, saw what she did.[NOTE:2]
notes: Or “I said to her, ‘Come back to me!’” The verb אָמַר (ʾamar) usually means “to say,” but here it means “to think,” of an assumption that turns out to be wrong (so HALOT 66 s.v. אמר 4) (cf. Gen 44:28; Jer 3:19; Pss 82:6; 139:11; Job 29:18; Ruth 4:4; Lam 3:18).sn Open theists suggest that passages such as this indicate God has limited foreknowledge; however, more traditional theologians view this passage as an extended metaphor in which God presents himself as a deserted husband, hoping against hope that his adulterous wife might return to him. The point of the metaphor is not to make an assertion about God’s foreknowledge, but to develop the theme of God’s heartbreak due to Israel’s unrepentance.
The words “what she did” are not in the text but are implicit from the context and are supplied in the translation for clarification.

verses.zh: 背道的以色列行淫，我为这缘故给她休书休她；我看见她奸诈的妹妹犹大，还不惧怕，也去行淫。
verses.en: She also saw[NOTE:1] that, because of wayward Israel’s adulterous worship of other gods,[NOTE:2] I sent her away and gave her divorce papers. But still her unfaithful sister Judah was not afraid, and she too went and gave herself like a prostitute to other gods.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “she [‘her sister, unfaithful Judah’ from the preceding verse] saw” with one Hebrew ms, some Greek mss, and the Syriac version. The MT reads, “I saw,” which may be a case of attraction to the verb at the beginning of the previous verse.
Heb “because she committed adultery.” The translation is intended to spell out the significance of the metaphor.

Heb “she played the prostitute there.” This is a metaphor for Israel’s worship; she gave herself to the worship of other gods like a prostitute gives herself to her lovers. There seems no clear way to completely spell out the metaphor in the translation.

verses.zh: 因以色列轻忽了她的淫乱，和石头木头行淫，地就被玷污了。
verses.en: Because she took her prostitution so lightly, she defiled the land[NOTE:1] through her adulterous worship of gods made of wood and stone.[NOTE:2]
notes: The translation reads the form as a causative (Hiphil, תַּהֲנֵף, tahanef) with some of the versions in place of the simple stative (Qal, תֶּחֱנַף, tekhenaf) in the MT.
Heb “because of the lightness of her prostitution, she defiled the land and committed adultery with stone and wood.”

verses.zh: 虽有这一切的事，她奸诈的妹妹犹大还不一心归向我，不过是假意归我。这是耶和华说的。」
verses.en: In spite of all this,[NOTE:1] Israel’s sister, unfaithful Judah, has not turned back to me with any sincerity; she has only pretended to do so,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “And even in all this.”
Heb “has not turned back to me with all her heart but only in falsehood.”

verses.zh: 耶和华对我说：「背道的以色列比奸诈的犹大还显为义。
verses.en: Then the Lord said to me, “Under the circumstances, wayward Israel could even be considered less guilty than unfaithful Judah.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Wayward Israel has proven herself to be more righteous than unfaithful Judah.”sn A comparison is drawn here between the greater culpability of Judah, who has had the advantage of seeing how God disciplined her sister nation for having sinned and yet ignored the warning and committed the same sin, and the culpability of Israel, who had no such advantage.

verses.zh: 你去向北方宣告说：耶和华说：背道的以色列啊，回来吧！我必不怒目看你们；因为我是慈爱的，我必不永远存怒。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: “Go and shout this message to my people in the countries in the north.[NOTE:1] Tell them: ‘Come back to me, wayward Israel,’ says the Lord.‘I will not continue to look on you with displeasure.[NOTE:2] For I am merciful,’ says the Lord.‘I will not be angry with you forever.
notes: Heb “Go and proclaim these words to the north.” The translation assumes that the message is directed toward the exiles of northern Israel who have been scattered in the provinces of Assyria to the north.
Heb “I will not cause my face to fall on you.”

verses.zh: 只要承认你的罪孽，就是你违背耶和华―你的　神，在各青翠树下向别神东奔西跑，没有听从我的话。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: However, you must confess that you have done wrong[NOTE:1] and that you have rebelled against the Lord your God.You must confess[NOTE:2] that you have given yourself to[NOTE:3] foreign gods under every green treeand have not obeyed my commands,’ says the Lord.
notes: Heb “Only acknowledge your iniquity.”
The words “You must confess” are repeated to convey the connection. The Hebrew text has an introductory “that” in front of the second line and a coordinative “and” in front of the next two lines.

Heb “scattered your ways with foreign [gods]” or “spread out your breasts to strangers.”tc MT reads דְּרָכַיִךְ (derakhayikh, “your ways”), but the BHS editors suggest דּוֹדַיִךְ (dodayikh, “your breasts”) as an example of orthographic confusion. While the proposal makes sense, it remains a conjectural emendation since it is not supported by any actual manuscripts or ancient versions.

verses.zh: 耶和华说：背道的儿女啊，回来吧！因为我作你们的丈夫，并且我必将你们从一城取一人，从一族取两人，带到锡安。
verses.en: “Come back to me, my wayward sons,” says the Lord, “for I am your true master.[NOTE:1] If you do,[NOTE:2] I will take one of you from each town and two of you from each family group, and I will bring you back to Zion.
notes: Or “I am your true husband.”sn There is a wordplay between the term “true master” and the name of the pagan god Baal. The pronoun “I” is emphatic, creating a contrast between the Lord as Israel’s true master/husband versus Baal as Israel’s illegitimate lover/master. See 2:23-25.
The words “If you do” are not in the text but are implicit in the connection of the Hebrew verb with the preceding.

verses.zh: 我也必将合我心的牧者赐给你们。他们必以知识和智慧牧养你们。」
verses.en: I will give you leaders[NOTE:1] who will be faithful to me.[NOTE:2] They will lead you with knowledge and insight.
notes: Heb “shepherds.”
Heb “after/according to my [own] heart.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说：「你们在国中生养众多；当那些日子，人必不再提说耶和华的约柜，不追想，不记念，不觉缺少，也不再制造。
verses.en: In those days, your population will greatly increase[NOTE:1] in the land. At that time,” says the Lord, “people will no longer talk about having the ark[NOTE:2] that contains the Lord’s covenant with us.[NOTE:3] They will not call it to mind, remember it, or miss it. No, that will not be done anymore![NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “you will become numerous and fruitful.”
Or “chest.”

Heb “the ark of the covenant.” It is called this because it contained the tables of the law, which in abbreviated form constituted their covenant obligations to the Lord (cf. Exod 31:18; 32:15; 34:29).
Or “Nor will another one be made”; Heb “one will not do/make [it?] again.”

verses.zh: 那时，人必称耶路撒冷为耶和华的宝座；万国必到耶路撒冷，在耶和华立名的地方聚集。他们必不再随从自己顽梗的恶心行事。
verses.en: At that time the city of Jerusalem[NOTE:1] will be called the Lord’s throne. All nations will gather there in Jerusalem to honor the Lord’s name.[NOTE:2] They will no longer follow the stubborn inclinations of their own evil hearts.[NOTE:3]
notes: For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
Heb “will gather to the name of the Lord.”
Heb “the stubbornness of their evil hearts.”

verses.zh: 当那些日子，犹大家要和以色列家同行，从北方之地一同来到我赐给你们列祖为业之地。」
verses.en: At that time[NOTE:1] the nation of Judah and the nation of Israel will be reunited.[NOTE:2] Together they will come back from a land in the north to the land that I gave to your ancestors as a permanent possession.
notes: Heb “In those days.”
Heb “the house of Judah will walk together with the house of Israel.”

verses.zh: 我说：我怎样将你安置在儿女之中，赐给你美地，就是万国中肥美的产业。我又说：你们必称我为父，也不再转去不跟从我。
verses.en: “I thought to myself,[NOTE:1] ‘Oh what a joy it would be for me to treat you like a son![NOTE:2] What a joy it would be for me to give[NOTE:3] you a pleasant land,the most beautiful piece of property there is in all the world!’[NOTE:4] I thought you would call me ‘Father’[NOTE:5] and would never cease being loyal to me.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “And I myself said.” See note on “I thought that she might come back to me” in 3:7.

Heb “How I would place you among the sons.” Israel appears to be addressed here contextually as the Lord’s wife (see the next verse). The pronouns of address in the first two lines are second feminine singular, as are the readings of the two verbs preferred by the Masoretes (the Qere readings) in the third and fourth lines. The verbs that are written in the text in the third and fourth lines (the Kethib readings) are second masculine plural, as is the verb describing Israel’s treachery in the next verse.sn The imagery here appears to be that of treating the wife as an equal heir with the sons and of giving her the best piece of property.
The words “What a joy it would be for me to” are not in the Hebrew text but are implied in the parallel structure.
Heb “the most beautiful heritage among the nations.”
Heb “my father.”
Heb “turn back from [following] after me.”

verses.zh: 以色列家，你们向我行诡诈，真像妻子行诡诈离开她丈夫一样。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: But, you have been unfaithful to me, nation of Israel,[NOTE:1] like an unfaithful wife who has left her husband,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “house of Israel.”
Heb “a wife unfaithful from her husband.”

verses.zh: 在净光的高处听见人声，就是以色列人哭泣恳求之声，乃因他们走弯曲之道，忘记耶和华―他们的　神。
verses.en: “A noise is heard on the hilltops.It is the sound of the people of Israel crying and pleading to their gods.Indeed they have followed sinful ways;[NOTE:1] they have forgotten to be true to the Lord their God.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “A sound is heard on the hilltops, the weeping of the supplication of the children of Israel because [or indeed] they have perverted their way.” At issue here is whether the supplication is made to Yahweh in repentance because of what they have done or whether it is supplication to the pagan gods that is evidence of their perverted ways. The reference in this verse to the hilltops, where idolatry was practiced according to 3:2, and the reference to Israel’s unfaithfulness in the preceding verse make the latter more likely. For the asseverative use of the Hebrew particle (here rendered “indeed”) where the particle retains some of the explicative nuance, see BDB 472-73 s.v. כִּי 1.e and 3.c.
Heb “have forgotten the Lord their God.” But in view of the parallelism and the context, the word “forget” (like “know” and “remember”) involves more than mere intellectual activity.

verses.zh: 你们这背道的儿女啊，回来吧！我要医治你们背道的病。看哪，我们来到你这里，因你是耶和华―我们的　神。
verses.en: Come back to me, you wayward people.I want to cure your waywardness.[NOTE:1] Say,[NOTE:2] ‘Here we are. We come to youbecause you are the Lord our God.
notes: Or “I will forgive your apostasies.” Heb “I will [or want to] heal your apostasies.” For the use of the verb “heal” (רָפָא, rafaʾ) to refer to spiritual healing and forgiveness, see Hos 14:4.

Or “They say.” There is an obvious ellipsis of a verb of saying here since the preceding words are those of the Lord and the following are those of the people. However, there is debate about whether the people’s words are a response to the Lord’s invitation, a response which is said to be inadequate according to the continuation in 4:1-4, or whether they are the Lord’s model for Israel’s confession of repentance, to which 4:1-4 adds further instructions about the proper heart attitude that should accompany it. The former implies a dialogue with an unmarked, twofold shift in speaker between 3:22b-25 and 4:1-4, while the latter assumes the same main speaker throughout, with an unmarked instruction only in 3:22b-25. The latter disrupts the flow of the passage less and appears more likely.

verses.zh: 仰望从小山或从大山的喧嚷中得帮助，真是枉然的。以色列得救，诚然在乎耶和华―我们的　神。
verses.en: We know our noisy worship of false gods on the hills and mountains did not help us.[NOTE:1] We know that the Lord our God is the only one who can deliver Israel.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Truly in vain from the hills the noise/commotion [and from] the mountains.” The syntax of the Hebrew sentence is very elliptical here.
Heb “Truly in the Lord our God is deliverance for Israel.”

verses.zh: 从我们幼年以来，那可耻的偶像将我们列祖所劳碌得来的羊群、牛群，和他们的儿女都吞吃了。
verses.en: From earliest times our worship of that shameful god, Baal, has taken away[NOTE:1] all that our ancestors[NOTE:2] worked for.It has taken away our flocks and our herdsand even our sons and daughters.
notes: Heb “From our youth the shameful thing has eaten up….” The shameful thing is specifically identified as Baal in Jer 11:13. Compare also the shift in certain names such as Ishbaal (“man of Baal”) to Ishbosheth (“man of shame”).
Heb “fathers” (also in v. 25).

verses.zh: 我们在羞耻中躺卧吧！愿惭愧将我们遮盖；因为从立国（原文是幼年）以来，我们和我们的列祖常常得罪耶和华―我们的　神，没有听从耶和华―我们　神的话。
verses.en: Let us acknowledge[NOTE:1] our shame.Let us bear the disgrace that we deserve.[NOTE:2] For we have sinned against the Lord our God,both we and our ancestors.From earliest times to this very daywe have not obeyed the Lord our God.’
notes: Heb “Let us lie down in….”
Heb “Let us be covered with disgrace.”
